statement: Share an open solo project to a chosen BIMcloud server and folder, optionally uploading its linked libraries, so permitted users can then open or join it.
superiority: Sharing is reversible and the project remains a plain file with open schema.

acceptance.sketch: Share project, open from second client: both see the same model; share is refused for a user without rights.

notes: CORRECTED — read Share a Teamwork Project; Share dialog picks BIMcloud, user, folder, name, host server and library handling; per-user roles are assigned in BIMcloud Manager, not in this dialog.

statement: Open a shared project from BIMcloud and receive a local copy that synchronises.

source.ref: Teamwork > Open or Join Teamwork Project

superiority: Fast partial join with streaming of model parts.

acceptance.sketch: Join gives all elements and all attributes of the latest version.

notes: VERIFIED — read Open or Join Teamwork Project and Join or Leave a Teamwork Project; joining keeps a local copy synchronised on send/receive; same Archicad version required for all members.

statement: Reserve elements for exclusive editing, with reservation visible to others via user colours.
superiority: Fine-grained reservation by element, property or region with automatic negotiation.

acceptance.sketch: User A reserves a wall; user B cannot edit it and sees the owner name.

notes: VERIFIED — read Feedback on Element Ownership and Reserve Elements by Selection; Colored Workspaces can show reservations per user colour, plus Info Tag states (Editable / Reserved by / Free).

statement: Release reserved elements to allow others to edit them after Send.

source.ref: Teamwork > Release Elements or Project Data (Teamwork)

superiority: Auto-release on idle with notification.

acceptance.sketch: After release user B can reserve and edit.

notes: VERIFIED — read Release Elements or Project Data; changes must be sent before a modified element is released (Send and Release prompt); pending requests are auto-granted on release.

statement: A user requests elements reserved by another user; the owner is notified, can grant or deny, and a grant releases the items so they are instantly reserved by the requester.

source.ref: Teamwork > Request Elements or Project Data (Teamwork)

superiority: Requests carry a timeout and auto-grant rule for idle owners.

acceptance.sketch: A requests wall owned by B, B grants: A can edit after B sends; decline leaves ownership unchanged.

notes: CORRECTED — read Request Elements or Project Data; grant transfers reservation immediately (not on next send); requester can revoke a pending request; request carries an attached view.

statement: Send local changes to the server, optionally adding a comment to the project activity log and notifying chosen users by message.
superiority: Atomic transactions with automatic conflict preview.

acceptance.sketch: Changes appear in other client after Receive.

notes: CORRECTED — read Send/Receive Changes and Add Comment to Activities; optional comment goes to the BIMcloud Activities panel; release is a separate command or close option; send clears the undo queue.

statement: Receive changes from others since the last receive and merge them into the local copy.
superiority: Background receive with non-blocking update.

acceptance.sketch: After receive, local model equals the server for non-reserved elements.

notes: VERIFIED — read Send/Receive Changes in Teamwork; only changes since the last receive are fetched, unsent local changes stay intact after a receive.

statement: One command sends local changes and then receives remote changes, in that order, so a user ends synchronised after a single action.
superiority: Background continuous sync with an explicit checkpoint action, so users rarely have to remember to sync.

acceptance.sketch: After Send and Receive on two clients with disjoint edits, both models hash equal.

notes: VERIFIED — read Send/Receive Changes in Teamwork and Teamwork Palette; the Send & Receive button runs both commands; strict send-before-receive order is implied by the palette wording, not spelled out.

statement: Attribute types are shared project data that must be reserved per type (or all types at once) before they can be modified or deleted, while any user can create new attributes and send them.

source.ref: Teamwork > Reservation in Attributes palette; Reserve All Attributes (Teamwork)

superiority: Attribute edits are merge-aware, not exclusive.

acceptance.sketch: Editing a locked attribute is refused for non-owner.

notes: CORRECTED — read Reservation in Attributes palette and Creating and Sending Project Data; reservation by attribute type with control lights; 'attribute locking' wording not used by help.

statement: Views, layouts, master layouts, subsets, publisher sets and schedule schemes are reserved individually, separately from model elements.
superiority: Item level locking visible in the tree.

acceptance.sketch: Layout reserved by A cannot be edited by B.

notes: CORRECTED — read Reserving Teamwork Project Data (Non-Elements) and its child pages (views, layout book items, publisher sets, interactive schedules); drawings are covered under layout items.

statement: Project-wide settings dialogs act as shared items with a status light and a Reserve button; changes made while reserved are sent to the server when released or sent.

source.ref: Teamwork > Feedback on Ownership of Teamwork Project Data

superiority: Settings as mergeable data.

acceptance.sketch: Settings change denied without reservation.

notes: CORRECTED — read Feedback on Ownership of Teamwork Project Data; blue/green/red control light on dialogs; 'Project Preferences' not named explicitly, Model View Options cited as example of project data.

statement: A palette shows joined users, workspace reservations, messages and tracked project changes, with online/offline status and send/receive/reserve controls.
superiority: Presence indicators with live cursors.

acceptance.sketch: Palette lists users and counts.

notes: CORRECTED — read Teamwork Palette; four panels: Workspace, Users, Messages, Project Changes; roles/ownership not shown as a single table.

statement: Roles are named permission sets granted to users or groups per project, folder or server (including view-only roles), controlling what each person may do in the project.
superiority: Role-based access by element class.

acceptance.sketch: Read-only user cannot reserve.

notes: CORRECTED — read Manage BIMcloud roles (BC help); roles are custom permission sets, not fixed Administrator/Read-only/Full; SaaS ships default groups (Archicad - Architect etc.); view-only roles possible.

statement: Send messages to team members, and receive notices on changes and reservation requests.
superiority: Threaded messages linked to elements.

acceptance.sketch: A message sent to B is delivered and flagged unread until opened.

notes: VERIFIED — read Messaging (Teamwork) and Create a New Message; context-driven text messages, offline delivery later, request messages automatic; no attachments or hyperlinks.

statement: Send a review message about selected elements to chosen users, with an attached view and element count that the recipient can show with one click.
superiority: Threads linked to elements.

acceptance.sketch: A chat message is delivered and linked to an element.

notes: CORRECTED — read Review Elements (Teamwork) and Messaging; a free-form project chat is not documented, only messages with element review and optional task buttons.

statement: Because modifying shared elements requires reserving them first and reservation needs an up-to-date local copy, edits in a local copy cannot conflict with server data.
superiority: Conflicts shown with 3-way diff.

acceptance.sketch: Edit on element reserved by other is refused.

notes: CORRECTED — read Teamwork Palette and Overview of Teamwork Reservation; help states no conflicts arise between local and server edits; ownership clashes are handled by Request.

statement: Work offline on a joined project from the local copy and later go online and run send and receive to bring local and server data back in step.
superiority: Longer offline windows with merge.

acceptance.sketch: Offline edits sync after reconnect.

notes: CORRECTED — read Working Online/Offline in Teamwork and Send/Receive; reserve, send/receive and messaging need online; '14 days SaaS' limit is not stated in AC30 or BIMcloud help.

statement: Roll a project back to an earlier snapshot on the same BIMcloud, either overwriting the current project or creating a new project from the snapshot.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > Restore data from snapshots

superiority: Named versions and diff.

acceptance.sketch: Restored state matches stored checkpoint.

notes: VERIFIED — read Restore data from snapshots (BC help); rollback overwrites or creates new project; all users must re-join after overwrite.

statement: Open only chosen stories, views or element types of a shared project to reduce load time and memory.

source.ref: Teamwork > Open or Join Teamwork Project

superiority: Streaming open without a separate partial mode, loading what the view needs.

acceptance.sketch: Partial open of one story loads only that story and memory use is lower than a full open.

notes: REJECTED: no partial-open of a Teamwork project by story/view/element type found in AC30 or BIMcloud help (only DWG/XREF layer partial open exists); searched open/partial/selected terms.

statement: Send and receive transfer only data changed since the last synchronisation, so network time scales with the amount of change rather than model size.
superiority: Delta-only sync with parallel compression.

acceptance.sketch: Change one element in a 100k-element project: send time stays within the performance budget.

notes: VERIFIED — read Send/Receive Changes in Teamwork and BIMcloud Features and Benefits; Delta Server technology limits traffic to changes only.

statement: Create issues that highlight elements and views, with status, priority, type, responsible person and due date.
superiority: Open issue standard (BCF API).

acceptance.sketch: Issue created and visible to others.

notes: CORRECTED — read Issue Details and Issue Handling; Archicad calls them Issues (not markup entries); assignment is on a separate page (see Assign Issue to User).

statement: Administrate servers, projects, users, groups, roles and licences via a browser manager.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > Working in BIMcloud Manager

superiority: API-driven administration.

acceptance.sketch: Create user and project; privileges respected.

notes: VERIFIED — read Working in BIMcloud Manager and Manage BIMcloud users and groups; web-based manager for projects, users, roles, servers and licences.

statement: Libraries used by a shared project are hosted on the BIMcloud and added through the Library Manager so every user, including offline ones, has the same parts.
superiority: Library versions pinned per project.

acceptance.sketch: A library update on the server reaches all clients after receive.

notes: CORRECTED — read Libraries in Teamwork and Libraries Setup for Teamwork Project Sharing; linked libraries are uploaded on share; library versioning/automatic loading not described.

statement: A cloud-hosted shared project can be edited disconnected for up to 14 days, after which sync is required.
superiority: Offline windows without hard expiry, with merge of non-overlapping edits instead of reservation-only.

acceptance.sketch: Edit offline, reconnect before the limit: changes sent; after the limit the client refuses edits.

notes: REJECTED: the 14-day offline limit is not stated anywhere in AC30 Teamwork or BIMcloud help; offline work itself exists (see TEAM-0017).

statement: Opening and working in the same shared project from a second computer without sending first raises an editing-conflict warning, and continuing discards the unsent edits of the first session.

source.ref: Teamwork > Avoid Conflicting Work Sessions in Teamwork Projects

superiority: Conflicts shown as a three-way diff instead of refusal.

acceptance.sketch: Edit of an element owned by another user is refused with the owner named.

notes: CORRECTED — read Avoid Conflicting Work Sessions in Teamwork Projects; options are discard-and-quit, discard-and-reopen, or save as solo project; reservation conflicts are separate (TEAM-0016, 0005).

statement: Colour the model by reservation status, either by owning user or as own/free/others, in 2D, 3D and schedule windows.
superiority: Presence and ownership shown on all views.

acceptance.sketch: Each user's reserved set shows in a distinct colour and counts match the palette.

notes: CORRECTED — read Feedback on Element Ownership; Colored Workspaces options (Highlight my reservation, Show Reservation by Users, etc.); filtering the selection by owner not documented.

statement: Save the local copy of a shared project as a solo project file for archive or for consultants without server access.

source.ref: Teamwork > Save Local Copy of Teamwork Project

superiority: Solo export includes history metadata on request.

acceptance.sketch: The solo file opens offline with all elements and attributes.

notes: VERIFIED — read Save Local Copy of Teamwork Project; Save as PLN produces a solo file; also PLN snapshots on BIMcloud can be reopened solo.

statement: Restore a BIMcloud Server or Manager from a stored server backup file after reinstalling it.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > How to restore backup for BIMcloud Server or Manager

superiority: Named versions with diff before restore.

acceptance.sketch: After restore the model hash equals the stored checkpoint hash.

notes: CORRECTED — read How to restore backup for BIMcloud Server or Manager; restore needs same build, uses tray icon Restore from Backup; project-level rollback is TEAM-0018.

statement: Assign an issue to a Teamwork user, who is notified by message and becomes its owner for handling in Issue Organizer.

source.ref: Issue Handling > Assign Issue to User

superiority: Issues use the open BCF API so third-party tools stay in sync.

acceptance.sketch: An issue created by A is visible to B with its element link.

notes: CORRECTED — read Assign Issue to User; assignment goes through Teamwork Messaging; 'due date' lives in Issue Details (see TEAM-0021).

statement: Roles hold predefined permissions per data type, such as creating or deleting and modifying layouts, views, attributes and publisher sets, that decide what a user can do in Teamwork.
superiority: Role rules by element class and phase.

acceptance.sketch: A read-only user cannot reserve or send; a full user can.

notes: CORRECTED — read Archicad-related permissions and Management-related permissions; permissions are per data type (create / delete-modify / manage), not a generic reserve/send switch.

statement: Layouts, views, schedules and project preferences are reserved separately from model elements.
superiority: Item-level locks visible in the navigator tree.

acceptance.sketch: Layout reserved by A refuses edits from B.

notes: VERIFIED — read Reserving Teamwork Project Data and Reserve Settings of Layout Book Items; overlaps TEAM-0010, kept separate as listed; project preferences not explicitly named.

statement: A palette lists joined users with online status, the current user's reservations, pending requests and messages, and tracked project changes.
superiority: Presence with live cursors.

acceptance.sketch: Palette lists all members and counts of reserved elements.

notes: CORRECTED — read Teamwork Palette and Review Your Workspace; Workspace, Users, Messages and Project Changes panels; overlaps TEAM-0012.

statement: Attribute types are reserved as a whole through the Attributes palette and new attributes created without reservation stay local until sent.

source.ref: Teamwork > Reservation in Attributes palette; Reserve All Attributes (Teamwork)

superiority: Attribute edits merge without exclusive reservation.

acceptance.sketch: New surface by A appears for B after receive with the same name.

notes: CORRECTED — read Reservation in Attributes palette and Creating and Sending Project Data; automatic merge on receive is not described; creation without reservation is.

statement: The project library is loaded from the server so all users see the same parts.
superiority: Library versions pinned per project.

acceptance.sketch: A library part update reaches all clients after receive.

notes: VERIFIED — read Libraries in Teamwork; BIMcloud Libraries plus Embedded Library are shared via the server so all users, including offline ones, have the same library parts.

statement: Browser manager to administrate servers, projects, users, groups, roles and licences.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > Working in BIMcloud Manager

superiority: All admin functions are available through an OpenAPI-described REST interface.

acceptance.sketch: Create user and project via the manager; privileges are respected on a client login.

notes: VERIFIED — read Working in BIMcloud Manager; browser interface for servers, projects, users, groups, roles and licences; duplicates TEAM-0022 in intent.

statement: Deployment choices are BIMcloud SaaS (hosted), on-premises BIMcloud, and the reduced-feature BIMcloud Basic.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > BIMcloud vs. BIMcloud Basic: Feature Differences

superiority: Open protocol enabling self-hosted servers.

acceptance.sketch: The same client connects to each deployment type.

notes: VERIFIED — read BIMcloud vs. BIMcloud Basic: Feature Differences, Welcome to BIMcloud and Welcome to BIMcloud SaaS; Basic lacks detailed permissions, delta cache, backups etc.

statement: Server computes differences between versions to cut traffic for send and receive.

source.ref: Teamwork > Graphisoft BIMcloud: Features and Benefits

superiority: Open delta format with resumable transfers.

acceptance.sketch: Delta transferred bytes are smaller than a full copy for a small edit.

notes: VERIFIED — read Graphisoft BIMcloud: Features and Benefits; Delta Server technology limits network traffic to changes; BIMcloud Delta Cache is an optional caching component.

statement: Snapshots of projects and libraries are created on an hourly or daily schedule per folder or project with a keep-last-N retention rule and can be rolled back.
superiority: Immutable versioned history by default.

acceptance.sketch: A restored backup equals the saved version.

notes: CORRECTED — read Schedule automatic snapshots and Restore data from snapshots; retention is keep-last-N; 'restore wizard' is the Rollback dialog; whole-server backups are separate.

statement: Create public links with optional password and expiry so people outside the team can download shared files, folders or projects without a BIMcloud account.
superiority: Expiring signed links with audit.

acceptance.sketch: Link opens a viewable model for a guest.

notes: CORRECTED — read Public links (SaaS help); guests download shared content, disabled by default; a read-only model viewer without licence is not described there.

statement: Server exposes an API for projects, users, jobs and status.
superiority: Public OpenAPI with SDKs.

acceptance.sketch: An API call lists the projects of the server.

notes: UNVERIFIED — searched BIMcloud help for REST/API; no API page in reachable BIMcloud or AC30 help; developer documentation is on unreachable hosts.

statement: An activities log and a server activity monitor show project, user and server events with filters and CSV export.
superiority: Prometheus compatible metrics.

acceptance.sketch: Metrics endpoint returns session count.

notes: CORRECTED — read Monitor BIMcloud activities; Activities panel plus graphical Activity Monitor for servers; resource monitoring is a full-BIMcloud feature; session/storage gauges not described.

statement: Existing elements are reserved automatically when a user starts modifying them, with a setting to switch this off and warnings when the elements belong to someone else or need a receive first.
superiority: Automatic reservation can be undone atomically and surfaces the blocking owner in the warning itself.

acceptance.sketch: Select an unreserved element and start a move: it becomes reserved by the actor; with auto-reserve off the same edit is refused until Reserve is used; an element reserved by another user yields a warning naming the owner.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Overview of Teamwork Reservation; auto-reserve is not available in BIMcloud Basic and is toggled in Data Safety & Integrity preferences.

statement: Reserve all elements matching criteria inside a chosen project region, such as selected stories or the active window, without selecting them.
superiority: Criteria reservation can preview the matching count and conflicts before committing.

acceptance.sketch: Define a region of one story and a criterion of walls: exactly the walls of that story become reserved by the actor and nothing is selected; elements already owned by others are listed as conflicts.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Reserve Elements by Criteria (Teamwork); criteria act as a filter, not a selection.

statement: After a reserve attempt with conflicts, a results palette lists per project region and data group how many items were reserved or blocked, and offers show, release and request actions.
superiority: The conflict list can be filtered by owner and exported as a to-do list.

acceptance.sketch: Reserve a region where 3 of 10 elements belong to another user: results show 7 reserved and 3 conflicts for that region; Show Conflict selects exactly the 3; Request creates one message for their owner.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Reservation Results (Teamwork); groups are project regions, navigator items, attribute types, library and other settings.

statement: An owner can assign elements directly to another user, who is notified by message and must receive pending changes before editing them.
superiority: Assignment can carry a task and due date visible in the recipient's workspace.

acceptance.sketch: Owner A assigns 5 elements to B: ownership becomes B, B receives one message, and B cannot edit them until a receive brings the latest data.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Assign Elements (Teamwork); the owner is prompted to send first if elements are not up to date.

statement: A permitted administrator can force a user out of a project from the Teamwork palette or the server manager, discarding that user's reservations and blocking unsent changes.

source.ref: Teamwork > Force User to Leave a Teamwork Project

superiority: Force-leave can offer to rescue the user's unsent changes as a recoverable branch.

acceptance.sketch: Force user U to leave: all reservations of U become free, U's later send is refused, and U can re-join unless removed from the project user list.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Force User to Leave a Teamwork Project and BIMcloud Force users to leave Teamwork project; multi-select and force-leave-all exist in the manager.

statement: An administrator can lock a project so joined users cannot send, receive or change data until it is unlocked, and migration locks it automatically.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > Lock or unlock a Teamwork project

superiority: Locking can show the reason and expected unlock time to joined users.

acceptance.sketch: Lock a project: send, receive and edits are refused for joined users and the project shows a lock badge; unlock restores normal operation.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Lock or unlock a Teamwork project (BC help); locked state also shown in the Open/Join dialog.

statement: Users subscribe to changes in elements chosen by criteria, selection or project data type, optionally filtered by team and user, and get notifications for changes sent by others until they receive them.

source.ref: Change Tracking in Teamwork > Subscribe to Changed Elements - by Criteria

superiority: Subscriptions can be shared as team-level watch rules with digest notifications.

acceptance.sketch: Subscribe to load-bearing elements; another user sends a change to one: subscriber gets a notification listing the changed parameter, which clears after the subscriber receives.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Change Tracking in Teamwork, Subscribe to Changed Elements by Criteria/Selection, Subscribe to Changes in Project Data and View and Manage Tracked Changes; not in BIMcloud Basic.

statement: After a receive or send and receive, compare the new local state with the previous local copy and see new, modified and deleted 3D elements in a separate compare window.

source.ref: Model Compare > Compare Teamwork Model Versions (Before and After Receiving Changes)

superiority: Compare results can be turned straight into review assignments per author.

acceptance.sketch: Receive a change that adds one wall and moves a slab: the compare view lists 1 new and 1 modified element and nothing for unchanged ones; 2D elements are not considered.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Compare Teamwork Model Versions and Model Compare; only 3D elements are compared.

statement: A travel pack bundles the local project and libraries so a user can continue on another computer, offline or alternating between locations, and merge back on the next send and receive.

source.ref: Teamwork > Travel Pack: Move Your Teamwork Project and Libraries to a Different Computer

superiority: The pack can be signed and checked for matching build before opening elsewhere.

acceptance.sketch: Create a pack, open it on a second machine with the same program build, edit, then send and receive: edits merge into the server project; a different build is refused.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Travel Pack page; requires identical program version and build on both computers.

statement: A local data manager lists the project and library copies stored on the machine with status and size, lets the user move the data folder, delete old copies and schedule cleanup reminders.
superiority: Cleanup can be previewed with the unsent-change risk per project.

acceptance.sketch: List shows each local project with size and server availability; deleting a copy removes only that local data and leaves reservations, while leaving the project also releases them.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Manage Local Teamwork Data, Delete Local Teamwork Data and Schedule Teamwork Data Cleanup Reminder.

statement: Snapshots come in three kinds: server-readable project snapshots with user data, library snapshots, and solo-file snapshots that open in the desktop program without rollback.
superiority: Every snapshot kind can be opened read-only for inspection without rollback.

acceptance.sketch: Create a project snapshot and a solo snapshot: the solo one opens as a standalone file; the project one only restores through rollback; library snapshot rollback leaves parts free of reservations.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Types of snapshots (BC help); reservation data is ignored when rolling back library snapshots.

statement: Server and manager components can be backed up on an hourly or daily schedule or manually, with a status of the last backup and a documented restore into a reinstalled server of the same build.
superiority: Backups can be verified automatically by a test restore.

acceptance.sketch: Schedule an hourly backup: backup files appear and the last-backup status reports success or error; restore on a same-build install recovers the data, a mismatched build is refused with the needed build number.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Server Backups and How to restore backup for BIMcloud Server or Manager (BC help); backups require configuration at install time; not in BIMcloud Basic.

statement: Administration offers a simple mode with two fixed management roles and a detailed mode where administrators define any number of management roles per content type.

source.ref: BIMcloud Help > Management permissions: Simplified and Detailed

superiority: Detailed management can be previewed as an effective-permission matrix per user.

acceptance.sketch: In simple mode a project administrator can view but not edit servers and roles; switching to detailed mode allows a custom role limited to modifying one folder's content.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Management permissions: Simplified and Detailed and Simplified management (BC help); Basic has only simplified mode.

statement: An optional cache component stores project data already downloaded by one client near the clients and serves the same data to the next client that asks for it.
superiority: Cache hits can be reported per project to show saved bandwidth.

acceptance.sketch: Client A downloads a project part through the cache, client B requests the same part: the cache serves it without a new server transfer of that part.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read BIMcloud Delta Cache (BC help); not available in BIMcloud Basic.

statement: In the hosted service, users, groups and licences are managed in the company account and synced to the server, and guest users from other companies can join with their own portable licence.

source.ref: BIMcloud SaaS Help > BIMcloud SaaS with cloud license

superiority: Guest access can be time-boxed per project with automatic expiry.

acceptance.sketch: Add a user to a company group: the user appears in the server with that group's roles; a guest with a portable licence can join a project granted to them and nothing else.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read BIMcloud SaaS with cloud license and Default user groups on BIMcloud SaaS (BCSAAS help); older Archicad versions need legacy authentication.
